checks.invariant: A GUI input (click/type/key) must not execute unless a burst baseline (workspace manifest + uid-1001 pid set) opened successfully, and the failure must be audit-recorded.
checks.result: service.py:250-265 closes the previous burst, takes the snapshot, calls mark_snapshot then GuiBursts.open; when open returns False it resets the timers and raises SandboxError before _run_tool, so the input is never sent. gui_bursts.py:71-74 records gui_burst_open_failed with snapshot_id and error and returns False instead of installing an empty baseline. The empty-baseline half of the run-3 record is also gone: workspace_manifest now raises on a nonzero exit (sandbox.py:379-380) and desktop_processes now raises on a nonzero exit (sandbox_desktop.py:56-57), so open() cannot silently collect nothing.

checks.invariant: Every principal that can invoke a GUI tool must reach the same snapshot/burst gate; no sibling route may bypass _snapshot.
checks.result: api.py:215-221 is the only tool route. agent.py:89 and mcp_server.py:87 both call that HTTP route and web.py has no tool route, so every GUI input goes AgentBox.call_tool (service.py:268) -> _call_tool (290) -> _needs_snapshot (239-240) -> _snapshot (343-345). GUI tools also share the per-sandbox _snap_locks entry (service.py:278-284).

checks.invariant: Burst close must record the manifest diff, must record an explicit failure when comparison is impossible, and must disclose truncation.
checks.result: _finish (gui_bursts.py:113-135) logs gui_burst_close_failed when the container id changed (115-119) or the close manifest cannot be read (121-124), and logs gui_changes with counts, at most 100 paths per category and a truncated flag (127-135). workspace_manifest raises on a nonzero exit and caps the listing at 8 MiB (sandbox.py:372-381); _parse_manifest sets truncated at the cap and drops an incomplete trailing record (gui_state.py:20-29).

checks.invariant: The stray kill must report what actually happened; a failed container-side kill must not be indistinguishable from a successful one.
checks.result: kill_processes (sandbox_desktop.py:64-67) discards the exec exit status and _stop_strays (gui_bursts.py:85-92) logs gui_processes_stopped for every selected pid, so a kill that never ran would still produce a success-shaped record. No attacker-reachable trigger was established: gui_strays only selects uid 1001, the kernel enforces the uid for kill -KILL, kill cannot be refused, and the container pid limit keeps the argv small. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate; this is the surviving part of run-3 record agentbox/service.py:_open_gui_burst:silent-fail-open-without-audit, whose open and collection halves are now fixed.

checks.invariant: GUI input must always leave a recovery point and a change record unless the operator deliberately disables it, and disabling must be visible.
checks.result: gui_bursts.py:55-57 returns False when gui_snapshot_interval <= 0, which skips _snapshot entirely: no snapshot, no burst open, no gui_changes, while mark_input still runs. config.py:51 defaults to 600 s and only AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL can set 0, so this is operator-supplied configuration with no startup warning. Hardening only.

checks.invariant: Control-plane-launched uid-1001 helpers (the x11vnc relay) must not give container code a reachable way to obtain a stray-kill exemption.
checks.result: vnc_command (sandbox_desktop.py:131-144) runs docker exec -i -u desktop <cid> socat - EXEC:x11vnc ...: the RFB byte stream is the exec stdio, so no port or socket exists in the container for a uid-1001 client to reach, and the relay runs with the attacker's own uid 1001 authority. The relay and its children are from_exec-exempt by design (gui_state.py:72-76) and only the authenticated control-plane relay consumes them. The recon lead (x11vnc remote-control used from inside the container to spawn processes under the exempt relay) is disproved for this deployment; absent -noremote/-safer (sandbox_desktop.py:138-139) remains a hardening note.

checks.invariant: _parse_ps must not accept attacker-chosen records: a container process must not be able to add a line with chosen pid/ppid/sid/uid through its argv.
checks.result: Started children whose argv contained a newline, CR, VT, FF, FS, GS, NEL and U+2028 followed by a forged record, then read the real ps -eo pid=,ppid=,sid=,uid=,args= bytes: procps-ng 4.0.4 replaced every control character with ? or space and emitted exactly one line per process, and _parse_ps returned one record per child with its real pid/ppid/sid/uid. The hypothesized ps-text injection (which would have let uid-1001 code forge the ancestor that makes from_exec() true, or forge a uid to redirect the kill) is disproved for this stack, so the line model in gui_state.py:41-49 has no injectable field.

checks.invariant: A uid-1001 process must be spared by the stray kill only for a control-plane-verifiable reason.
checks.result: With procs = session leader 100 (uid 1001) -> shell 150 -> daemon 160 and baseline {100,150}: gui_strays(procs, set(), base) returned [160]; gui_strays(procs, {160}, base) returned [] - the daemon is spared solely because its pid is in window_pids although 160 owns no window; when only baseline ancestor 150 is in window_pids the daemon is still killed. desktop_processes (sandbox_desktop.py:59-61) builds window_pids from the decimal tokens of xdotool getwindowpid over xdotool search --onlyvisible --name ., i.e. from the client-set _NET_WM_PID property, with no check that the pid owns a window or that the declaring client is that process. Carried as the needs_validation candidate.

checks.invariant: The from_exec exemption (ppid 0) must identify only control-plane docker-exec roots and must not be attacker-reachable.
checks.result: Observed inside the sandbox: the docker-exec'd root appeared as '1 0 1 65534 /usr/bin/timeout -k 5 120 /usr/bin/python3 /scratch/h_ps.py' (ppid 0) exactly as exec_root (gui_state.py:72-76) assumes, and a normally spawned child chain was 9->7->1->0. Orphans are reparented to PID 1 inside the pid namespace, so a uid-1001 process cannot acquire ppid 0 itself; combined with the disproved ps injection the exemption is not forgeable by container code.

checks.invariant: The manifest parser must not let container-controlled metadata forge or hide records, and truncation must be visible.
checks.result: _parse_manifest (gui_state.py:17-29) consumes NUL-separated 4-field records; a Linux filename cannot contain NUL, so a path cannot inject or shift fields, the incomplete tail record is dropped (21) and truncated is set at the 8 MiB cap (20). diff_manifest (32-35) compares only (size, mtime, ctime) equality. Residual hardening: workspace_manifest runs find ... | head -c through sh -c (sandbox.py:376-378), so the pipeline status is head's and a find failure returns 0 with a partial manifest and truncated=False; missing entries can only mislabel a change as added/deleted, never as unchanged, so no hiding path was found.

candidates.title: GUI burst stray kill spares any uid-1001 process whose pid is named in the client-declared _NET_WM_PID window list
candidates.description: When a GUI burst closes, GuiBursts stops the uid-1001 processes that appeared during the burst so that GUI-launched background work cannot keep changing /workspace outside the policy and outside any gui_changes record. Whether a process counts as a windowed app is decided from window_pids, which desktop_processes fills with the decimal output of xdotool getwindowpid. That is the _NET_WM_PID property, which the X client sets itself; nothing binds the spared pid to a window or to the client that owns it. A uid-1001 process in the desktop session can therefore map a one-pixel titled window and set its _NET_WM_PID to the pid of a second process that has no window at all, and that second process survives every burst close while continuing to write /workspace between bursts, where no manifest diff observes it.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The stray-kill exemption is derived from container-declared X window metadata instead of a control-plane-verifiable link. sandbox_desktop.desktop_processes (sandbox_desktop.py:59-61) turns every decimal token printed by xdotool getwindowpid into a window pid, gui_state.gui_strays (gui_state.py:85-86) spares a new uid-1001 process when its pid or a new ancestor pid is in that set, and gui_bursts._stop_strays (gui_bursts.py:83-85) then kills only the remaining pids. Because _NET_WM_PID is written by the X client and any desktop-session process can reach the display (images/desktop/agentbox-desktop-start:19-21,30,38), the attacker chooses which of its processes are treated as windowed apps, so the burst-end kill no longer bounds what keeps running.

trace.description: The agent (agt_ token, prompt-injectable) sends click/type to a desktop sandbox. GUI input is policy-free by design and executes as uid 1001 in the desktop session (sandbox_desktop.py:45-47, 94-129).
_needs_snapshot is true for GUI input, so _snapshot (250-265) takes the recovery snapshot and opens a burst whose baseline is the workspace manifest plus the current pid set (gui_bursts.py:65-77).
The typed command runs in the desktop session as uid 1001 and starts a background process that never opens a window, staying in the baseline session id.
When the burst closes (close_idle, gui_bursts.py:137-155) the strays are collected and killed before the closing manifest is read.

window_pids is the set of decimal tokens of xdotool getwindowpid for every visible named window, i.e. the client-declared _NET_WM_PID values; any integer is accepted and no window ownership is verified.
A new uid-1001 process is spared when its pid is in window_pids, or when a new ancestor pid is, regardless of which process actually owns that window.
kill_processes receives only the unexempted pids, so the attacker's daemon survives the burst and keeps modifying /workspace between bursts, where no burst baseline or diff observes it.

evidence.description: The windowed test reads only window_pids (client-declared) plus a new-windowed-ancestor heuristic; there is no binding between the spared pid and the window's owning client.
The only other exemptions are baseline pids, pid 1, non-1001 uids and from_exec, so for a same-session process the window test is the sole gate.
The docstring states the window set is the _NET_WM_PID of visible windows, which X clients write themselves.
xdotool getwindowpid output is split and filtered by isdigit only; nothing checks that the pid owns a window or is the declaring client.
Xvfb and the Xfce session are started as the desktop account (uid 1001) via setpriv, so any process in that session can connect to :0 and set window properties.
startxfce4 runs as the desktop account, which is the identity the agent's typed GUI input inherits.
The stated purpose of the kill is to stop work that would otherwise keep changing files outside policy after the burst ends, which this exemption defeats.
Only the selected pids are logged as gui_processes_stopped, so a spared daemon leaves no failure record and the absent pid is the only hint.

blockers: The decisive platform step - a uid-1001 X client setting _NET_WM_PID to another process's pid and xdotool getwindowpid reporting it - needs a live X server. The approved sandbox has no X server, no Xvfb and no X11 client library, so the property-trust step cannot be observed locally.
Observing the spared daemon after a real idle close needs the Docker-backed desktop container (docker exec for ps, xdotool, kill and the socat/x11vnc relay); the sandbox forbids the Docker daemon.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable desktop-image container with network none, start the desktop, then as the desktop account run a helper that maps a 1x1 titled window and sets _NET_WM_PID to the pid of a second 'sleep 300' process started with & (same session id, no window). With the audited tree, call SandboxManager.desktop_processes(sid) and gui_state.gui_strays(procs, wins, baseline=current pids minus the daemon) and assert the daemon pid is absent from the result while the same call with wins=set() contains it; then call kill_processes(sid, result) and assert the daemon is still running.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a disposable desktop sandbox with dummy files: drive the agent's type/click to start 'nohup sh -c "sleep 300" &' plus the window helper before AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_IDLE (60 s) elapses, then read GET /audit: the gui_processes_stopped record for that close must omit the daemon pid and an exec ps must still show it running, with no later gui_changes row for its writes. Audit reads only; the process and files are dummy.

hardening: agentbox/sandbox_desktop.py:64-67 discards the kill exec exit status while agentbox/gui_bursts.py:85-92 logs gui_processes_stopped for every selected pid; read the status (and stderr) and log a failure reason, so an image without a reachable kill or a vanished pid cannot produce a success-shaped burst record.

agentbox/sandbox.py:376-378 runs find ... | head -c through sh -c, so the pipeline status is head's; a find failure still returns exit 0 with a partial manifest and truncated=False. Use set -o pipefail or check PIPESTATUS[0] and mark the record truncated.

agentbox/gui_bursts.py:55-57 plus agentbox/config.py:51: AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=0 silently disables the snapshot and the burst record for all GUI input; reject 0 at config load or log a startup warning so a GUI audit trail cannot be switched off unnoticed.

agentbox/service.py:250-265 opens a burst without the gui_lock, so a takeover that closes the burst in between (service.py:514) leaves a baseline that predates the human's own changes and their edits are recorded as agent gui_changes. Same burst-open/close ordering family as the h-gui-race unit; noted for routing, not claimed here.

agentbox/sandbox_desktop.py:138-139 runs x11vnc without -noremote and -safer; the only RFB peer is the authenticated control-plane relay over exec stdio and its uid-1001 authority is what a takeover already grants, so no boundary is crossed, but both flags are free.
